PLAN "2-Week Travel Maintenance (Hypertrophy Hold)"
TYPE workout
VISIBILITY public

GOALS
  GOAL primary strength:
    name "Maintain hypertrophy readiness while traveling"

PHASES
  PHASE "Phase 1" (2 weeks):
    WEEK 1:
      DAY Monday training 30m "Upper body sustain and core":
        warmup:
          walking 5 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          push_up 3x12 rpe 7 rest 60 seconds
          pull_up 3x6..8 rpe 7 rest 90 seconds
          incline_press 3x10 rpe 7 rest 75 seconds
          dumbbell_row 3x12 rpe 7 rest 75 seconds
        cooldown:
          chest_stretch 5 minutes
          shoulder_stretch 5 minutes
      DAY Tuesday training 30m "Lower body and core":
        warmup:
          jog_in_place 5 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          goblet_squat 3x12 rpe 7 rest 60 seconds
          hip_thrust 3x12 rpe 7 rest 75 seconds
          lunges 3x10 each leg rpe 7 rest 60 seconds
          dead_bug 3x12 each side rpe 6 rest 45 seconds
        cooldown:
          hamstring_stretch 5 minutes
          hip_flexor_stretch 5 minutes
      DAY Wednesday training 20m "Active recovery & mobility":
        warmup:
          marching 3 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          hollow_hold 3x20 seconds rpe 5 rest 30 seconds
          glute_bridge 3x15 rpe 6 rest 45 seconds

          jumping_jack 5 minutes

PLAN "Travel Nutrition Guidance for 2-Week Maintenance"
TYPE guidance
VISIBILITY public

GOALS
  GOAL primary nutrition:
    name "Simple travel-friendly eating approaches for maintenance days"

PHASES
  PHASE "Phase 1" (2 weeks):
    WEEK 1:
      DAY Monday guidance "Travel day eating strategy":
        description:
          - Focus on protein-rich, balanced meals to support maintenance.
          - Aim for ~1.6–2.2 g protein per kg body weight daily; distribute across meals.
          - Prioritize familiar, protein-forward options at restaurants or room service.
          - Hydration: target 2–3 liters water per day; limit alcohol; watch sodium.
        recommendations:
          - breakfast: egg-based or yogurt + fruit + whole-grain option; add protein (e.g., omelet, Greek yogurt parfait).
          - lunch: grilled chicken/fish/salmon or plant protein, vegetables, whole grain or legumes; avoid heavy fried items.
          - dinner: lean protein + vegetables + complex carb (brown rice, quinoa, potato) when available.
          - snacks: Turkey/chicken slices, fruit, nuts, protein shake if available.
          - beverage: water, unsweetened tea; coffee as desired.
      DAY Tuesday guidance "Hotel dining options":
        description as above with emphasis on restaurant/room service menus.
      DAY Wednesday guidance "Light training day, restaurant choices":
        description as above.
      DAY Thursday guidance "Push protein first":
        description as above.
      DAY Friday guidance "Seafood or lean protein focus":
        description as above.
      DAY Saturday guidance "Work demands, convenient options":
        description as above.
      DAY Sunday guidance "Relaxed travel day":
        description as above.
    WEEK 2:
      DAY Monday guidance ...
    (Repeat Week 1 structure or adapt to travel schedule; keep protein-centered, portion-controlled meals.)

NOTES:
- Keep meals simple: choose a protein source first, then add vegetables and a carb portion.
- If room service: order a la carte with protein-heavy items (grilled chicken/fish, eggs, legumes), sides of vegetables, and a modest portion of carbohydrates.
- When dining out: look for bowls or plates that include a protein, veggies, and a carb; avoid oversized meals and heavy fried items.
- Protein targets are general; adjust to client’s typical intake and appetite. Hydration emphasized.

PLAN "Travel Hold Weekly Metric for 2-Week Maintenance"
TYPE guidance
VISIBILITY public

GOALS
  GOAL primary guidance:
    name "Simple weekly metric to monitor maintenance during hold block"

PHASES
  PHASE "Phase 1" (2 weeks):
    WEEKLY_METRICS
      - metric_name: "weekly_bodyweight"
        description: "Change in bodyweight from start of week to end of week"
        unit: "lbs"
        target_trend: "within +/-2.0% of starting bodyweight for the week"
      - metric_name: "training_volume_stability"
        description: "Total planned training reps/sets completed vs plan"
        unit: "percent"
        target_trend: ">= 90%"
      - metric_name: "protein_intake_consistency"
        description: "Estimated daily protein intake adherence"
        unit: "percent"
        target_trend: ">= 80%"
      - metric_name: "cardio_finisher_adherence"
        description: "Completion rate of 15-minute cardio finishers"
        unit: "percent"
        target_trend: "100% on scheduled days"
      - metric_name: "perceived_exertion_consistency"
        description: "Average RPE across sessions compared to plan"
        unit: "points (1-10)"
        target_trend: "within +/-1 of planned RPE average"

RECORDING
  - method: "weigh-in once per week (same time, same scale)"
  - method: "log training completion against plan (Yes/No, % of sessions completed)"
  - method: "log approximate daily protein target achievement (Yes/No, estimate)"
  - method: "log cardio finishers completed (Yes/No, 15 minutes)"
  - method: "note any deviations (reason)"
  
IMPLEMENTATION NOTES
  - Use a simple spreadsheet or note app to track weekly values.
  - Define week boundary (e.g., Monday to Sunday) for consistency.
  - If weight fluctuates, consider small weekly delta tolerance; visuals (green/yellow/red) can help maintain motivation.
  - Ensure privacy and client comfort with tracking; emphasize data for maintenance, not judgment.
